title: You didn’t wake up believing lies.
paragraphs: You didn’t wake up believing lies.
You absorbed them.
Quietly. Repeatedly. Through screens, songs, conversations, and applause. Until what once felt wrong started feeling normal… and what God calls truth started feeling extreme.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
A lie doesn’t need to sound evil to destroy you. It just needs to sound right.
And some of the most celebrated ideas in culture are directly pulling your soul away from the One who made you.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
You’ve heard it before—maybe you’ve even said it:
“Just follow your heart.”
It sounds freeing. Honest. Empowering.
But God says something very different:
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?” (Jeremiah 17:9)

Your heart doesn’t lead you to truth. It leads you to what feels good in the moment. And you’ve seen it—how feelings shift, how desires contradict themselves, how what once satisfied you left you emptier the next day.
God saw it.
You knew.
Following your heart without truth doesn’t lead to freedom. It leads to confusion… then compromise… then consequences.
And still, culture keeps repeating it like a mantra.
Another lie comes dressed as self-love:
“You are enough.”
It sounds comforting. It feels like healing.
But it quietly removes your need for a Savior.
Scripture doesn’t flatter your condition—it exposes it:
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
You weren’t created to be enough on your own. You were created to depend on God.
And the moment you start believing you’re self-sufficient, you stop seeking the One who can actually save you.
This is where the lie becomes dangerous—it replaces grace with pride.
Then there’s the one that never gets challenged:
“Do what makes you happy.”
It feels harmless… until happiness becomes your authority.
But Jesus never said chase happiness. He said:
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.” (Luke 9:23)
Deny yourself.
That doesn’t trend well. That doesn’t go viral.
But it’s the path to life.
Because what makes you happy today might destroy you tomorrow.
Sin often feels good before it kills something in you.
Read that again.
Another lie sounds almost spiritual:
“Live your truth.”
But truth isn’t something you create.
Jesus said, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.” (John 14:6)
Not a truth.
Not your version.
The truth.
When everyone defines truth for themselves, deception multiplies. And you start justifying things God clearly calls sin.
You start bending Scripture to fit your life instead of surrendering your life to Scripture.
And deep down… you feel the tension.
You know when something is off.
Because truth isn’t subjective—it’s a Person. And His name is Jesus Christ.
Then comes the final lie—the one that keeps people stuck the longest:
“God just wants you to be happy.”
No.
God wants you to be holy.
“Be holy, for I am holy.” (1 Peter 1:16)
Holiness doesn’t always feel good. It requires surrender, repentance, obedience.
But it leads to something deeper than happiness—it leads to transformation.
To peace that isn’t dependent on circumstances.
To joy that survives suffering.
To a life that actually means something.
And this is where everything shifts.
Because once you see the lies… you can’t unsee them.
The question is what you’ll do next.
Will you keep agreeing with a culture that’s constantly changing… or will you anchor yourself to a God who never does?
Because the Gospel isn’t about making your life more comfortable.
It’s about saving your soul.
You’ve sinned. That’s the truth culture avoids.
But God didn’t leave you there.
“God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Jesus lived the life you couldn’t live… and died the death you deserved.
Not to improve you.
To redeem you.
To pull you out of deception and into truth.
To break the cycle.
To give you a new heart—not one you follow blindly, but one transformed by His Spirit.
And now you’re standing at a decision point.
Not emotionally.
Spiritually.
Because hearing truth and ignoring it only hardens you.
You feel that weight right now.
That tension.
That conviction.
This is where people either turn… or turn away.
If something in you is recognizing the lies you’ve been living under, don’t keep it hidden.
Say it.
Type it.
“I’ve been believing lies, and I need truth.”
Not for me.
For you.
And if you know someone who is drowning in these same deceptions, don’t stay silent. Send this to them. Because silence doesn’t save people—truth does.
There’s a deeper walk waiting for you—one that corrects you, builds you, and leads you into real freedom in Christ. That’s what you step into when you commit to growing, not just consuming.
Because truth isn’t just something you hear.
It’s something you live.
And the life you choose from this moment forward… will prove what you actually believe.
